findings.description: The lane-to-catalog matching key is undefined, so 'catalog-derived cost projections for every configured dispatch lane' cannot be met. model_catalog rows are keyed (vendor, model, endpoint_kind) where vendor is the OpenRouter slug ('anthropic', 'openai') or 'local'; AgentEntry carries type='claude_code', cli.model=null for claude-local (resolved later via archetypes.yaml), and sdk.model='claude-sonnet-4-6' with endpoint_kind unset. No existing mapping joins vendor_type to catalog vendor, so every CLI lane would project cost=unknown and the 'Catalog pricing is available' policy scenario can never fire in production.
findings.resolution: Specify the join in D3: which AgentEntry fields (cli.model, cli.model_fallbacks, sdk.model, archetype-resolved model, endpoint_kind) become the candidate model set, and a deterministic vendor_type→catalog-vendor mapping owned by the registry (or by agents.yaml). Add a test that claude-local and codex-local resolve to non-empty catalog projections against a seeded catalog.

findings.description: Watchdog probe persistence (tasks 3.1/3.2, 'Watchdog records a probe') will never run in the deployed coordinator. WatchdogService._check_vendor_health loads skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/vendor_health.py by filesystem path and silently returns when it is absent; the production Dockerfile copies only skills/shared/github_classifier.py, so the file does not exist in the container and every lane stays 'unknown' (and is excluded from available_only reads).
findings.resolution: Either COPY vendor_health.py into the image and add it to the check_docker_imports data list, or move the probe into agent-coordinator/src (with vendor_health.py importing it) and put that path in wp-api-producers write_allow. Add a Docker smoke test asserting the probe module resolves.

findings.description: No work package can edit the code that actually observes rate limits, so task 3.6 'Ingest dispatcher-observed limits' has no caller. vendor_limit_reporter.py is a new file in wp-bridge-policy, but provider_dispatch.py (skills/autopilot/scripts, provider strings 'claude_code'/'codex'), review_dispatcher.py (_CAPACITY_PATTERNS, SdkRateLimitError), and the autopilot-roadmap SKILL.md prompt layer that emits 'vendor_limit:<vendor>:<reason>' are all outside every write_allow. The only in-scope caller is orchestrator.py, which sees a free-text vendor token, not a lane.
findings.resolution: Add provider_dispatch.py and review_dispatcher.py (plus their tests) to a producer package, or add an explicit 'wp-dispatch-reporting' package, and define the ordering so the reporter is called from the dispatch result path with the selected agent_id.

findings.description: Three vendor namespaces collide and the plan defines no translation: roadmap policy and _STATIC_COST_TIERS use 'claude'/'codex'/'pi'; provider_dispatch and AgentEntry.type use 'claude_code'; lane IDs are 'claude-local'/'claude-remote'. D7 says alternates are 'grouped by vendor type' (claude_code) but Policy.preferred_vendor and VendorLimit.vendor arrive as 'claude', so preferred_vendor matching, the limited-lane exclusion, and static-tier fallback all silently miss. The legacy 'vendor_limit:claude' outcome therefore cannot become an unambiguous lane observation without a documented resolution rule.
findings.resolution: Define one canonical provider key for policy (recommend AgentEntry.type) and a deterministic legacy alias table ('claude'→'claude_code'); specify that a provider-only limit with multiple matching lanes is applied to the lane that dispatched (from context) or, if unknown, is rejected and logged, and add tests for preferred_vendor under both spellings.

findings.description: 'Registry is unavailable → bounded injected fallback provider or fail closed' regresses the common local runtime. autopilot-roadmap runs with the host LLM as runtime and frequently no coordinator (this session reports Transport: none); today _handle_vendor_limit always has five alternates, so a rate limit yields a switch. After removal of the roster, an unreachable coordinator with no injected provider turns every vendor limit into fail_closed, halting roadmap execution.
findings.resolution: Specify the default fallback concretely: derive alternates from local agents.yaml via get_dispatch_configs/vendor_health when the coordinator is unreachable, mark the decision source as 'fallback' in policy_decisions, and add an orchestrator test that a coordinator-down vendor limit still produces a switch.

findings.description: A rate-limit observation with reset_at NULL (allowed by the contract and by RateLimitObservation, where both reset_at and retry_after_seconds are optional) is 'active' forever under D4, so one unbounded observation permanently excludes a lane until an operator deletes the row. This contradicts the proposal's 'expired limits stop excluding lanes without operator repair'.
findings.resolution: Require a bounded window: either make reset_at NOT NULL (server computes it from retry_after_seconds or a documented default such as 15 minutes), or add a stale_after column and treat NULL-reset rows as expired after it. Add a test for the no-reset case.

findings.description: Staleness is asserted but never defined. D4 says 'missing or stale evidence is unknown' and the probe table has stale_after, yet nothing states who sets stale_after or its relationship to VENDOR_HEALTH_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 5 min). The spec requirement 'Live Availability State' omits the stale-to-unknown transition entirely, so it is untested by the spec.
findings.resolution: State that the watchdog writes stale_after = observed_at + k × vendor_health_interval (k=2 or 3), add a 'Probe becomes stale' scenario to the spec, and make the injected clock test cover it.

findings.description: Lanes without a CLI section never get a probe. check_all_vendors skips agents without 'cli', and load_agents_yaml's HTTP path uses /agents/dispatch-configs which drops non-dispatchable entries, so SDK-only or routable-endpoint lanes (and ocr-local) stay 'unknown' forever and are excluded from available_only=true reads. dg-00 local probes already cover endpoint_kind='local' rows in the catalog, but D1 gives no rule for merging that signal into lane status.
findings.resolution: Specify per-lane evidence sources: CLI lanes from vendor_health, local/openrouter lanes from catalog available/stale, SDK-only lanes from api-key resolution; document that lanes with no evidence source are reported unknown and are NOT filtered by available_only unless a probe exists.

findings.description: Any valid API key can mark any lane limited for up to 7 days (retry_after_seconds max 604800) with an unbounded metadata object and a caller-chosen 'source'. Keys are registry-derived per agent with trust levels, but the plan does not bind the observation to the principal or gate by trust, so a trust-level-1 key can blackhole routing for every other agent.
findings.resolution: Record principal.agent_id alongside source, require a minimum trust level (or the lane's own key / watchdog identity) for writes, cap metadata size, and lower the retry_after ceiling to the longest real vendor window (24h).

findings.description: The OpenAPI contract declares BearerAuth only, but the bridge client (_http_request) sends X-API-Key and the coordinator's verify_api_key accepts Bearer, X-Coordinator-API-Key, and X-API-Key. Contract-parity tests written against v1.yaml will not describe how wp-bridge-policy actually authenticates, and D5's route naming ({lane_id}) differs from the contract and lock keys ({agent_id}).
findings.resolution: Add the X-API-Key apiKey security scheme as an alternative in v1.yaml (matching existing coordinator contracts) and align D5 to {agent_id}.

findings.description: retry_after_seconds has no anchor: the contract does not say whether reset_at = observed_at + retry_after (client clock, may be skewed or stale) or server receipt time + retry_after, nor which wins when both reset_at and retry_after_seconds are present. Also, replaying observation_id with a different agent_id is specified as 'idempotent' rather than a 409 conflict.
findings.resolution: Specify server-clock anchoring, precedence (explicit reset_at wins), and 409 on observation_id reuse with a different payload.

findings.description: D7's 'request-scoped price projection' has no deterministic reduction to the scalar policy.py needs. _estimate_cost_delta_with_source takes a vendor→float lookup; the registry returns per-model prompt/completion USD-per-Mtok lists. Which model per provider, which token assumptions, and how prompt vs completion combine are unspecified, so the resulting cost_ceiling decisions are not reproducible across runs.
findings.resolution: Define a quote rule: selected model if known else cheapest eligible catalog model for that vendor_type, fixed token assumption (e.g., 20k prompt / 4k completion, versioned), delta = to − from in USD, with source='catalog' provenance recorded on the PolicyDecision; keep set_catalog_pricing as the seam.

findings.description: wp-api-producers edits skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/vendor_health.py and its tests but its verification step runs only coordinator pytest, so a vendor_health regression passes the gate. wp-integration is tier A yet its only verification is 'openspec validate --strict', with no test or lint command, so the merged tree is never exercised by the package that claims full validation.
findings.resolution: Add skills/.venv pytest for test_vendor_health.py to wp-api-producers, and add the coordinator and skills test suites plus ruff/mypy to wp-integration's steps.

findings.description: Rate-limit ingestion emits nothing: the lock key names an event 'vendor.availabilityobserved' but no design decision emits it, no audit_log entry is written for POST observations, and expiry of a limit is silent. Operators cannot tell why a lane vanished from available_only reads or who reported it.
findings.resolution: Emit vendor.limited / vendor.limit_expired on the coordinator_agent channel (mirroring vendor.unavailable/recovered), audit-log ingestion with the principal, and include a 'reason_code' in Availability.

findings.description: GET /vendors naturally becomes per-lane catalog and rate-limit queries (CatalogService only exposes list_entries/get_entry), and vendor_rate_limits rows are never purged, so the (agent_id, reset_at) index scans grow without bound.
findings.resolution: Specify one list_entries call and one rate-limit query per read, and a watchdog cleanup of rows past reset_at + retention.
